body:
Triage: lands in `scripts/` (a new small docs-index gate) + the three landing pages; `pm:queue` · `domain:devx` · type Task. Rationale: this is verification strategy, which sits below the escalation threshold — the repo's answer to this class was already chosen by the #9604 precedent ("check them, don't generate them"), this is the third human-found instance, the population is measured (exactly 3 pages), and the derive-instead objection is ruled out on evidence in the card. The maintainer's veto window stays open via the round report. Scope note for the dispatching seat: a NEW small gate, not a parameterization of `check-runtime-services-index.mjs` (the card explains why); the #9465 fence workaround (lint.yml direct step, no package.json alias) is already precedented by PR #10698.

Size/model suggestion: S–M, `mode:subagent`, sonnet/opus; Clause-②: no.

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

**Population correction: the instance count is 4, not 3** — measured while implementing #10737 (PR #10747).

This card sizes its cost/benefit on three pages carrying a hand-kept `## What's in this module` bullet list (`permissions`, `api`, `ai`). Re-measuring every directory under `content/docs` that has both a `meta.json` and an `index.mdx`, there is a **fourth**:

| section | `meta.json` pages | linked in the list | missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ai` | 9 | 8 | 0 (after PR #10747) |
| `permissions` | 21 | 20 | 0 (after PR #10736) |
| `api` | 12 | 11 | 0 |
| **`plugins`** | **5** | **4** | **0** |

`content/docs/plugins/index.mdx` was not named in the original sweep. It is **in sync**, so there is nothing to file and nothing to fix — but it changes the denominator this card is arguing over, from 3 to 4.

Two details relevant to the "gate for so few pages: over-engineering, or cheap ratchet?" question:

1. **The population is growing, and nobody is counting it.** Two of the four were measurably drifted when someone finally looked, and the fourth went unnoticed by a sweep that was deliberately looking for exactly this shape. Whatever the right answer is, "we know how many there are" is not currently true without re-running a script.
2. **The four have four different textures**, which is direct evidence for *check, don't generate*: `ai` glosses 8 of 8 rows; `permissions` glosses 3 of 14; `api` glosses 11 of 11; `plugins` bolds its link text and capitalizes its glosses. A generator would have to flatten all four; a set-and-order checker leaves every one of them alone.

Method, if it is worth re-running: parse each directory's `meta.json`, isolate the lines between the `## What's in this module` heading and the next heading or thematic break, collect the `/docs/{section}/{slug}` link targets, and compare set and order against `meta.json` minus `index`. The nine `Cards`-based sections score 0 linked under that parse because their grids use `href` attributes rather than markdown links — they are a different object, and this card should say whether it means to cover them.

## ⚠️ Correcting my own card: the population is **4**, not 3

I filed this 20 minutes ago with *"exactly three pages"* in the body and **"3 known instances"** in the title. A dev agent working #10737 found a fourth while re-sweeping, and I have verified it myself on `origin/main` = `8163a1c8e2`:

| section | `meta.json` pages | linked | missing | hand-kept list | also has `<Cards>` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `permissions` | 21 | 14 | **6** | yes | no |
| `api` | 12 | 11 | 0 | yes | **yes** |
| `ai` | 9 | 7 | **1** | yes | no |
| **`plugins`** | 5 | 4 | 0 | **yes** | no |

`content/docs/plugins/index.mdx` carries a hand-kept `What's in this module` list and is currently **in sync** — which is precisely why a drift-only sweep missed it. **Title corrected to 4.**

Two things this changes, both in the proposal's favour:

- **The denominator is bigger than I priced it.** My "three pages may not be worth a gate" caveat was weighing the cost against 3; it is 4, and a fourth found *only* because someone swept for it rather than tripping over a defect.
- ⭐ **`api/index.mdx` carries a hand-kept list *and* a `<Cards>` block.** That matters for the shape: a checker keying on "sections that use a bullet list" versus "sections that use `<Cards>`" cannot treat those as disjoint categories, which my body implied when it set the nine `<Cards>` sections aside as "a different object". They overlap.

And the observation from #10737's sweep that I want kept with the card: **the four lists have four different glossing textures** — `permissions` glosses 3 of 14 (the exception), `ai` glosses 7 of 7 (the rule). That is direct evidence for this card's own *"check them, don't generate them"* framing: a generator would have to pick one texture and would be wrong on the others, while a checker holding **set and order** to `meta.json` is indifferent to how each page chooses to gloss.

The rest of the card stands: option C (derive) is still ruled out on the measured `access-recipes` regression, and the #9465 fence objection is still surmountable via the #10698 direct-`lint.yml` wiring.

Credit where due — the correction came from the #10737 dispatch's own repo-wide re-sweep, posted at [#10738 (comment)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/10738#issuecomment-5368621126), and it also confirmed no *undrifted-but-unfixed* instance exists beyond these.

⛔ Fenced OUT: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is owned this round by #10642 — `lint.yml` only. `packages/**` is owned by #10921.
Container & model: `S–M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — triage suggested S–M sonnet/opus on `5368584418`; taking **opus**, one step above the floor, because this round adds a population question the card had explicitly left open (below) and that is judgement, not a mechanical edit.
Clause-②: no — a new repo gate plus docs edits; no contract accept/reject behaviour, no public-surface widening. (Triage independently marked `Clause-②: no`.)
Serial constraints cleared: no open PR touches `scripts/**`, `lint.yml` or `content/docs/**`. The 6 open PRs (#11246, #11244, #11241, #11211, #11183, #10183) are all `packages/**` or Version Packages. Siblings in this batch are fenced disjoint: #10642 owns `ci.yml`, #10921 owns `packages/**` and is barred from `scripts/**` and root `package.json`.

## ⭐ New measurement — the population question this card left open is now answered, and the answer is "the `Cards` sections drift too"

The card sets the nine `<Cards>`-based sections aside as *"a different object, and no claim is made about them"*, and the correction on `5368651651` flags that `api/index.mdx` has **both**, so the two categories *"cannot be treated as disjoint… which my body implied"*. The card asks outright that someone *"say whether it means to cover them"*.

Measured on `origin/main` this round, and it is not hypothetical: **`content/docs/ui/index.mdx` is a `<Card>` section and it is drifted.** `content/docs/ui/meta.json` declares 17 entries; the landing page renders **11** `<Card>` rows and omits **`react-pages`, `actions`, `reports`, `translations`**.

That omission is not cosmetic — it is the **residual cause of a maintainer-reported symptom**. The report that opened P0 #10638 was *"`https://objectstack.ai/docs/ui` does not show the React Pages entry"*. The deploy half of that card is fixed and closed; the page is served and `react-pages` **is** in the sidebar payload. What is still missing, in production right now, is its row on the landing page — because the hand-kept `<Card>` grid never got it. Verified against a positive control: `grep -o 'href="/docs/ui/[a-z0-9-]*"'` on the served page returns eleven neighbours in exactly that spelling and no `react-pages`.

So the honest scope is that this gate cannot stop at the four bullet-list pages: excluding `<Card>` grids leaves unguarded the precise defect a human just reported.

⚠️ **Not a licence to force every grid to match `meta.json`.** The card itself records that some grids are deliberately curated — `protocol/objectui` is a *"For Implementers"* reading list mixing in `/docs/references/` links, `getting-started` deliberately links *out* of its module. Blanket set-and-order on those would be wrong. Weighing the shapes is part of the work; see the route block in the dispatch order, where it is marked as a suggestion to be beaten by measurement, not a ruling.

**ACCEPT** — PM review of record, PR #11259. Verified against GitHub and against the tree, not against the report's own account.

## Checked

**PR form.** Draft · base `main` · `Fixes #10738` on the first line · 5 files, all within the declared surface plus one declared deviation (below) · no changeset, `Check Changeset` **success** with `skip-changeset` — correct, since the diff touches `scripts/`, `lint.yml` and `content/docs/**` only, `@objectstack/docs` is `private: true`, and `content/docs` sits in no package.

**Path surface taken from `get_files`, not from the body.** `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, `content/docs/{ui,data-modeling,permissions}/index.mdx`, `scripts/check-section-landing-index.mjs`. **No governed path** (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) ⇒ ordinary landing, not the human-merge fork. Clause ② not reachable: no `packages/spec/src/**`, and the claim declared `Clause-②: no`.

**CI, read as named job conclusions rather than the aggregate.** `Lint & Repo Gates` — the job that carries the new step — **completed/success**. Also success: `Test Core` (rollup) and all six shards, `Build Docs`, `Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, and the three single-writer/claim guards. ⚠️ The `Vercel` commit status reads `Canceled by Ignored Build Step` — that is a **preview** deploy legitimately skipped, and it is the exact signal that was misread as the root cause on P0 #10638. Not a failure.

## The green was not taken on trust — I reproduced the red

A gate that cannot be shown failing is a belief, and CI can only ever show this one passing. So I ran it myself, in a throwaway worktree at the pre-fix commit:

```
$ git worktree add --detach <tmp> f5a52e13b     # gate present, docs NOT yet fixed
$ node scripts/check-section-landing-index.mjs

EXIT=1

$ node scripts/check-section-landing-index.mjs --self-test
✓ ... 31 assertions ... observed FAILING and observed silent.       EXIT=0
```

And the structural claim that makes that red *reproducible* rather than asserted checks out — commit 1 carries **only** `scripts/check-section-landing-index.mjs`; commit 2 carries the wiring and the docs fixes. Committing the gate ahead of the repair was a deliberate, and correct, choice.

## The measurement beat my dispatch, and that is the valuable part

My Zone-3 route proposed **two strengths** — set-and-order for the bullet lists, coverage-only for the `Card` grids. That is falsified and I am recording it as mine: order already held on **7 of the 8** sections, and the eighth is `ui`, the page the gate exists for.
